clue.text: Took notice of man with awful deed

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of deed are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man's terrible act finally gets attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' gives the pronoun, a common crossword shorthand, and 'awful' rearranges the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to pay attention to it, so the past tense is a synonym for took notice of.

clue.text: I reportedly will embrace vile malevolent gaze

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the word vile is held inside the other piece
reportedly signals a word as heard, so the letter I is taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter I is said the same way as the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be about to hug a wicked person despite their hostile stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the pronoun, but 'reportedly' makes it the organ of sight; 'will embrace' wraps that round the word vile.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a folk idiom for a malicious look believed to bring harm.

clue.text: Twelve work at Buddhist faith

parts.note: to do is to work or perform
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A dozen people labour at a Buddhist religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is a set of twelve, a simple numerical synonym.

clue.text: Lower the dignity of church official embracing me

indicators.note: embracing means holding, so the official's title wraps round the second piece

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric in charge of a cathedral

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a cleric hugging them is beneath their dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean is to degrade someone or make them lose respect.

clue.text: Nothing New York Times gave for stone

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing
the multiplication sign, read as times, looks like the letter X

explanation.surface: The New York Times paper reports on a gemstone, or gave nothing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semiprecious gem.

clue.text: Treading the boards, male only falls into one

indicators.note: falling into something puts it inside, so stag goes within the word one

parts.note: a stag event, like a stag party, is for men only

explanation.surface: An actor on stage, a man alone, tumbles into someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male only' gives STAG, as in a men-only stag party; it drops into ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading the boards is a theatrical idiom for performing in front of an audience.

clue.text: Long time before end of reign

indicators.note: before places the time word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word reign

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time ahead of the close of a monarch's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to pine or crave it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Loathe a taste of crab hors d'oeuvre

indicators.note: a taste is a small sample, so the letters are found within the words crab hors

explanation.surface: Someone hates a sample of crab served as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest something intensely, a synonym.

clue.text: Auctions off prison rooms, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: cells are the rooms inmates are held in

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a prison is putting its rooms up for auction.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a way of selling goods to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Left in pieces when hearing prolonged bombing

indicators.note: when hearing signals the result is taken by sound, so S becomes Z

parts.note: L, the abbreviation for left, goes inside BITS, small pieces, giving BLITS

explanation.surface: A building left in fragments after a sustained air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) sits in BITS (pieces) to make BLITS, and 'when hearing' turns that into the sound-alike word ending in Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blitz was the sustained German air campaign on Britain in 1940-41; the word now means any intense bombardment.

clue.text: Motorway share is an error

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
a take is one's share of the proceeds

explanation.surface: Sharing a motorway is a bad idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The M in British motorway names (M1, M25) supplies the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is a wrong action or judgement, a direct synonym for a slip.

clue.text: South Pacific islands seen from a canoe I upset

indicators.note: an upset canoe is capsized, so the letters a canoe I are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spotted Pacific islands after tipping their canoe over.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region taking in Australasia and the islands of the central and South Pacific.

clue.text: Cancel book, not author's first

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed from the book

parts.note: an annual is a book published yearly

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of author's

explanation.surface: A publisher scraps a book that wasn't the writer's debut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A, the first letter of 'author's', from ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, as with a contract or marriage, so it means cancel.

clue.text: Mushy peas containing one brown pigment

indicators.note: containing means holding, so the rearranged peas wrap round the numeral
mushy peas are mashed, so the letters of peas are mashed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bowl of mushy peas with a single dash of brown colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushy' turns PEAS into SEPA, and 'containing' puts I inside it. Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the reddish-brown pigment from cuttlefish ink, used for old photographs.

clue.text: Eroding ruin paid no heed

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters of eroding are broken up

explanation.surface: Wearing away left a building in ruins nobody cared about.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ignored something is to have disregarded it entirely.

clue.text: Lacerates eye secretions

definitions.meaning: to lacerate is to rip skin or cloth, the verb sense
drops of fluid from the eyes when crying, the noun sense

explanation.surface: Cuts that bring on crying.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling is two words: rips (rhyming with bears) and weeping drops (rhyming with fears).

clue.text: Reunite characters in train

indicators.note: characters are letters, so the letters of reunite are taken and reordered

explanation.surface: Bringing people back together inside a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests a railway, but here it means a group of followers. 'characters' rearranges REUNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a group of attendants following an important person, as a train is.

clue.text: Pay out to put page in post

indicators.note: put signals placing one piece somewhere, here inside the word for post
in says where the page abbreviation goes: within the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: Settling a bill by putting a sheet of paper in the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money is to pay it out.

clue.text: Council raged and held up bulb

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
held means contained, so the letters sit within the words Council raged

explanation.surface: An angry council objected and stopped a light bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' finds CILRAG inside 'Council raged', and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of the plant is technically a bulb, divided into cloves.

clue.text: Funny old penny loaf

parts.note: D was the symbol for a penny before British decimal currency in 1971
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: An old coin buys an amusing loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: D, from the Latin denarius, marked the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means dryly amusing or whimsical.

clue.text: Park throws out only tall supporter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for park, as on road signs

indicators.note: throwing out tosses things around, so the letters of only are jumbled

explanation.surface: A park keeper ejects the one tall fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall tower carrying power cables, so it holds them up.

clue.text: Arm over for bar dance?

parts.note: an arm is a limb
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Swapping a limb for a drink and a dance at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The limbo is danced by leaning back under a low bar, not in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a Caribbean dance in which dancers bend backwards to pass beneath a lowered pole.

clue.text: Accomplice has a chance to repent, initially

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken, a gamble

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of repent

explanation.surface: A criminal's partner gets an opportunity to feel remorse at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor helps or encourages someone to commit a crime, a partner in it.

clue.text: Small fish constantly circling lake

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the word for constantly surrounds the lake letter

parts.note: ever means always or constantly
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A little fish swims around and around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a small fish.

clue.text: Figure manure was spread on lake

indicators.note: manure spread on a field is scattered, so its letters are scattered

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A shape was made by muck spread beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a written figure or digit that represents a number.

clue.text: Mercenary victory on back road

parts.note: V stands for victory, as in the V sign

indicators.note: back means the word for road runs backwards

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A hired soldier wins on the road home.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal means open to bribery, motivated by money, like a hired fighter.

clue.text: Deity admits nothing fine

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the word for deity takes in the zero

parts.note: a deity is a god
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: A god confesses that nothing is all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and good are synonyms for satisfactory or of decent quality.

clue.text: Escort turns to supporter

indicators.note: turning means changing form, so the letters of escort become something new

explanation.surface: A chaperone looks to someone for backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a close-fitting undergarment that supports and shapes the body.
